newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese pilots resume flights after strike.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese pilots resume flights after strike.

text.p: Pilots at state carrier TAP-Air Portugal went back to work on Saturday after a 48-hour strike which grounded international flights and left around 14,000 passengers stranded.
A TAP spokesman said flights were operating normally but there were some delays and the airline had laid on extra flights to clear the backlog.

The Union of Civil Aviation Pilots (SPAC), which represents the company's 430 pilots, said talks to end the dispute over working hours were continuing and warned that there could be further stoppages if the company failed to meet its demands.
TAP, which the Socialist government wants to privatise next year, is seeking greater flexibility in working hours in an attempt to boost efficiency and cut costs.
But the pilots say that they already work more than colleagues with rival European airlines and that increasing their workload threatened the safety of planes.

TAP lost 10.5 billion escudos ($61 million) in 1996. It had been hoping to make a profit for the first time in 23 years in 1997 but the company says that the strike has cost some $6.0 million and may wipe out all the expected gain.
